title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is extremely faint pencil, and the machine transcription recovers only fragments. I have checked only its displayed formulas against the image. Everything below is therefore partly conjectural.

Context. The neighbouring pages are Grothendieck's copy or excerpt of Sullivan's construction of minimal models ('Infinitesimal computations', steps 1-2 and the inductive step). This French page sits between those English pages. It belongs to the dossier on the divided-power de Rham complex (IHES talk, 1976). That dossier is presumably about an integral, divided-power analogue of Sullivan's rational polynomial-forms model of cochains.

What the page appears to do.
(1) Cochains as maps into a cosimplicial object. Cochains of a simplicial set X_. with coefficients in a module M are written as maps into a cosimplicial (or graded) module C_M: C^n(X_.) = Hom(X_n, C^n_M). The page then wants to compute this representing object explicitly.
(2) The explicit description. The page writes C^n_M ~ M^{Hom(Delta_n, Delta_?)} ~ k^{Hom(Delta_n, Delta_?)} (x)_k M ~ (Lambda k^{Delta_n}) (x)_k M.
- The target simplex is hard to read; the transcription says Delta_{n+1}.
- The only reading that makes the last isomorphism dimensionally correct is Delta_1 with set-maps. Maps [n] -> {0,1} are subsets of [n]; there are 2^{n+1} of them, which is the rank of the exterior algebra on k^{[n]}. Monotone maps [n] -> [1] number only n+2.
- So the identification is presumably the standard one: functions on subsets of the vertex set are identified with the exterior algebra on the vertices, via the elementary cochains e_{i0...ip}.
(3) Introducing Omega. The page then writes C^._M ~ Lambda^. Omega_k (x)_k M. Here Omega_k is a cosimplicial k-module, something like n -> k^{Delta_n} (perhaps reduced). It comes with a map T: k -> Omega_k = C^1_k. A parenthetical seems to say Omega_k ~ k, presumably 'up to homotopy / after shift'.
(4) Projectivity and exterior powers. 'Or Omega_k ... projectif': Omega_k is (degreewise) projective. So exterior powers Lambda^i Omega_k (x) M behave well (are computed correctly, i.e. underived = derived). This leads to a statement 'Ainsi C^._M ...' identifying the full cochain object with an exterior algebra tensored with M.
(5) Last lines. These seem to concern a map C^._M -> C^{..}_{..}, a product or diagonal, 'compatible ...'. The reading is uncertain.

Interpretation. The page shows that the standard cosimplicial object computing cochains is, multiplicatively, an exterior algebra on a degreewise-projective cosimplicial module of 'degree-one cochains'. This is a cosimplicial/décalage-type fact. Under décalage, exterior powers of a shifted object become divided powers. This is the natural bridge from simplicial cochains to a divided-power de Rham complex over Z or k, replacing Sullivan's Q-polynomial forms.
errors: As transcribed, M^{Hom_Simp(Delta_n, Delta_{n+1})} cannot be isomorphic to (Lambda k^{Delta_n}) (x) M by a rank count. The intended object is presumably maps [n] -> {0,1} (subsets of the vertex set), i.e. Delta_1 with set-maps. This is either a transcription error or a slip in the notes.

Most of the argument is illegible, so the correctness of the claimed identification of the whole cochain object with Lambda Omega_k (x) M cannot be verified. Taken at face value it holds only up to the usual normalization and shift conventions.

ideas.what: Representing cochains C^n(X) = Hom(X_n, C_M) by a cosimplicial coefficient object.
ideas.modern_name: Cochains as maps into a cosimplicial (Eilenberg-MacLane) object; Dold-Kan

ideas.what: Identifying functions on subsets of the vertices of Delta_n with the exterior algebra on k^{Delta_n}, so that the cochain object is Lambda(Omega_k) (x) M for a projective cosimplicial module Omega_k with a unit map T: k -> Omega_k.
ideas.modern_name: Exterior-algebra description of simplicial cochains; décalage (Lambda^i of a shifted object vs divided powers / Sym)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dold-Puppe; Quillen; Illusie (Complexe cotangent, décalage isomorphisms)

ideas.what: Using this as a step toward an integral, divided-power analogue of Sullivan's polynomial de Rham model of cochains (context of the whole dossier and of the neighbouring Sullivan pages).
ideas.modern_name: Divided-power polynomial forms on simplices as an integral commutative model of cochains
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cenkl-Porter (integral de Rham with divided-power/tame forms, c. 1980s); related later work by Karoubi, Mandell (E_infinity cochains)
ideas.where_published: Only the title of the 1976 IHES talk is known from the archive inventory.

missed.claim: The page juxtaposes Sullivan's rational minimal-model construction with a cosimplicial exterior-algebra description of integral cochains. This suggests Grothendieck was seeking an integral, divided-power version of rational homotopy theory around 1975-76, before Cenkl-Porter and later integral models. The page itself is too illegible to establish any finished result.
missed.quote: C^{n}_{.M} ~ (Lambda k^{Delta_n}) (x)_k M ... Or Omega_k ... projectif
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of historical interest for the prehistory of integral or p-adic models of homotopy types. The ideas at stake are décalage, divided-power de Rham forms and E_infinity cochains. Mathematically the visible content is standard.

deep.surprise_reason: What is legible is a standard identification of the simplicial cochain object with an exterior algebra tensored with M, plus a projectivity remark. The context of an integral, divided-power analogue of Sullivan models is historically interesting. However, nothing on this page is clearly a new or uncredited result, and most of the text is illegible.
transcription_corrections: In the display, the exponent Hom_Simp(Delta_n, Delta_{n+1}) is probably not Delta_{n+1}. Comparing ranks with Lambda k^{Delta_n} requires maps [n] -> {0,1} (Delta_1, set-maps).
The superscript written 'n!' on C (C^{n!}) is probably a degree index together with a decoration such as a shriek or prime, not a factorial.
Lambda^{n} Omega_k (x)_k M is probably the full exterior algebra Lambda^. Omega_k (x)_k M, graded in degree n.
